newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: PLO urges U.N. Assembly to denounce Israel actions.
newsitem.headline: PLO urges U.N. Assembly to denounce Israel actions.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation urged the General Assembly on Wednesday to denounce Israel's plan to build new Jewish housing in mainly Arab East Jerusalem and other actions that it said violated U.N. resolutions and the peace process.

PLO U.N. observer Nasser al-Kidwa opened a debate in the 185-member assembly after the United States on Friday vetoed a Security Council resolution calling on Israel to abandon a project to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a tree-lined hill called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by Palestinians. It was captured by Israel during the 1967 war.
Israel considers Jerusalem its undivided capital while the Palestinians see East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.

The United States was among nearly 50 speakers in the council debate that denounced the Israeli action. But, casting the only negative vote, it said that body was not the place to deal with matters that should be negotiated by the two sides.

Speakers in the assembly were also virtually unanimous in criticising Israel and a resolution similar to the vetoed council draft was certain to be adopted by an overwhelming majority when put to a vote, probably on Thursday. There is no veto in the assembly, whose decisions are not binding.

Al-Kidwa said Israel aimed at "the Judaization of occupied East Jerusalem and at changing its legal status and its demographic composition," as well as continuing a "colonial settlement campaign" in the area it has occupied since 1967.

"All of these measures represent a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law and relevant United Nations resolutions and a breach of the agreements concluded within the framework of the Middle East peace process," he said.
Israeli U.N. envoy David Peleg said his government "does not regard the United Nations as the appropriate forum for discussing issues of contention between Israel and the Palestinians."

He said the multitude of U.N. resolutions on the Arab-Israeli conflict had "failed to advance the peace process even one inch" while direct negotiations, beginning with the 1991 Madrid conference, "have proven the only way to advance the cause of peace in our region."

Despite the progress achieved so far, whenever contentious issues had arisen recently the Palestinians had "run to third parties and bodies not involved in the peace process with the hope of imposing their positions on Israel," Peleg said.

He said Israel also had grievances "concerning Palestinian violations of our agreements" but preferred "not to misuse this body to air our concerns. We prefer to do so directly with the Palestinians, as agreed by the two sides."
